## Talent Is the Strategy

Warren Buffett once said, "Somebody once said that in looking for people to hire, you look for three qualities: integrity, intelligence, and energy." CEOs who internalize this — who make talent their primary strategic lever — consistently outperform their peers.

### The Data

A 10-year study of 500 companies found that organizations where the CEO spends 20%+ of their time on talent strategy:

- Grow revenue 2.2x faster than peers
- Have 34% higher employee engagement
- Achieve 41% higher customer satisfaction
- Experience 28% lower executive turnover

### The CEO Talent Framework

#### 1. Define Your Talent Philosophy

Every company needs a clear answer to: "What kind of people thrive here, and how do we find them?"

Want to see this in action?

Start a risk-free pilot for one role. Get a scored shortlist in 14 days with no placement fees.

[Start a pilot](/pilot)
[See how it works](/how-it-works)

This is not HR's job — it is the CEO's job to set the talent philosophy that HR executes.

#### 2. Build the Leadership Bench

| Planning Horizon | Focus |
|---|---|
| 0-6 months | Immediate succession for all C-suite roles |
| 6-18 months | Developing 2-3 candidates for each VP+ role |
| 18-36 months | Identifying high-potential individual contributors for leadership tracks |
| 3-5 years | Industry scanning for transformational leaders |

#### 3. Create Hiring Velocity

In fast-moving markets, the ability to hire quickly without sacrificing quality is a competitive moat. Key metrics:

- Time-to-offer: Target <21 days for most roles
- Offer acceptance rate: Target >85%
- Quality of hire (1-year retention + performance): Target >80%

Subscription sourcing models create this velocity by maintaining always-on talent pipelines.

#### 4. Measure What Matters

| Metric | Why It Matters | CEO Cadence |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue per employee | Productivity proxy | Quarterly |
| Regrettable turnover | Losing your best people | Monthly |
| Hiring plan attainment | Execution capability | Monthly |
| Diversity metrics | Innovation and fairness | Quarterly |
| Employee NPS | Culture health | Quarterly |

### The Cost of Getting It Wrong

A bad hire at the VP level costs 15-27x their salary when you factor in severance, replacement cost, team disruption, strategic delay, and opportunity cost. At the C-suite level, a wrong hire can derail a company for years.

Invest in strategic hiring partnerships that align incentives and quality.
